summary: John Powers specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at College of the Holy Cross, McMaster University, and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding positions at the Australian National University, Deakin University, and the University of Melbourne.

John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisors Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, alongside instruction from traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama.

John R. McRae (1947–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. His career included faculty posts at Cornell University, Indiana University Bloomington, Komazawa University, and the Numata Center.
John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who received traditional training under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ronald Newman is a specialist in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

John Ross Carter (1938–2020) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard University under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, and held a long-term academic appointment at Colgate University from around 1972 to 2010.

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After studying at Oberlin College, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds, he served as a professor at Bates College, alongside several visiting professorships.

John Shakespear (1774–1858) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under John Richardson. He held an orientalist professorship at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore (1751–1834) was an Indology and history scholar who served as President of The Asiatic Society, succeeding William Jones.

John Stratton Hawley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Amherst College and worked under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Bowdoin College (~1974–1977) before becoming a professor at Columbia University around 1986.
John Stuart Mill (1806–1873) was a philosopher who studied at University College London. He worked at the East India Company from around 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall (1878–1960) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Cambridge and Leiden University, founded the Burma Research Society in 1910, and held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1936 to 1940.

John Taber is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later holding faculty posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1982–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

John Thompson Platts (1830–1904) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he taught at Benares Sanskrit College and became Teacher of Persian at Oxford in 1880.
John Vincent Bellezza is a Tibetologist and archaeologist who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He held a post at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and completed doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman.

John W. Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his bachelor's and PhD at the University of Oregon under Don Levi, and joined the faculty at St. Mary's College of Maryland in 1996.

John W. Spellman (1934–2021) was an Indology and history scholar. He held an academic post at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Windsor (~1967–1999).

John Wilson (1804–1875) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

Join Saeki (1867–1952) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji under Jōchō Chihaya. He served as head of Horyu-ji (1903–1950) and held appointments at Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, and the Japan Academy (1929).
